name: Venice
hook: Marco Polo, the Doge, the Grand Canal and Shakespeare: six things cover almost every Venice clue.

facts.label: Marco Polo
facts.statement: Marco Polo was born in Venice in 1254; Kublai Khan used the Venetian as an envoy, and a biography is subtitled "From Venice to Xanadu."

facts.label: the Doge
facts.statement: The doge ruled Venice for 1,100 years, from Paolo Lucio Anafesto in 697 to Ludovico Manin, who abdicated in 1797.

facts.label: the Grand Canal
facts.statement: The Grand Canal runs about two miles in an S shape, with the Rialto Bridge over it and one end at St. Mark's Basilica.

facts.label: the Bridge of Sighs
facts.statement: The Bridge of Sighs inspired Byron's line about "a palace and a prison on each hand," and Cambridge, England named a bridge after it.

facts.label: The Merchant of Venice
facts.statement: In The Merchant of Venice, Portia speaks "The quality of mercy is not strained" and Shylock warns, "Since I am a dog beware my fangs."

facts.label: Thomas Mann
facts.statement: Thomas Mann wrote Death in Venice — "half fairy-tale, half snare" — and died in Switzerland in 1955.

facts.label: Othello
facts.statement: Othello opens in Venice, where the Duke summons Othello over a Turkish threat, then moves to Cyprus.
